Understanding 'Change of Heart'

The story describes how Prabhat, who always wanted to win and could not accept defeat, changed his attitude after playing against Surya. Initially, he felt terrible when losing and would only play if sure of winning. However, after observing Surya's enjoyment despite losing, Prabhat realized that enjoying a game is about trying well and having fun, not just winning or losing.

Key Vocabulary from the Chapter

The chapter introduces several important words: 'phenomenon' (someone with special qualities), 'tally of marks' (final marks on a report card), 'sporting spirit' (following rules and being fair), 'significant' (important), 'hopeless' (having no skill in something), and 'observed' (watched closely).

Prabhat's Attitude Before the Match

Before playing, Prabhat was very serious about winning. He would not play if he sensed he might lose, even for a short time. He only played games he was good at, like badminton, because he felt it was his duty to win.

Prabhat's Attitude After the Match

After losing, Prabhat did not feel happy or sad. He could not sleep well that night. However, he realized that to enjoy a game, you do not need a scoreboard or worrying about winning/losing; you just need to have fun.

The Lesson Learned

Through his observation of Surya playing basketball happily despite losing, Prabhat learned that sporting spirit is important because it involves following rules and being fair. He changed his heart from wanting to win at all costs to enjoying the game itself.

Understanding 'Change of Heart'

The story describes how Prabhat, who always wanted to win and could not accept defeat, changed his attitude after playing against Surya. Initially, he felt terrible when losing and would only play if sure of winning. However, after observing Surya's enjoyment despite losing, Prabhat realized that enjoying a game is about trying well and having fun, not just winning or losing.

Key Vocabulary from the Chapter

The chapter introduces several important words: 'phenomenon' (someone with special qualities), 'tally of marks' (final marks on a report card), 'sporting spirit' (following rules and being fair), 'significant' (important), 'hopeless' (having no skill in something), and 'observed' (watched closely).

Prabhat's Attitude Before the Match

Before playing, Prabhat was very serious about winning. He would not play if he sensed he might lose, even for a short time. He only played games he was good at, like badminton, because he felt it was his duty to win.

Prabhat's Attitude After the Match

After losing, Prabhat did not feel happy or sad. He could not sleep well that night. However, he realized that to enjoy a game, you do not need a scoreboard or worrying about winning/losing; you just need to have fun.

The Lesson Learned

Through his observation of Surya playing basketball happily despite losing, Prabhat learned that sporting spirit is important because it involves following rules and being fair. He changed his heart from wanting to win at all costs to enjoying the game itself.
